# Steven A. Rodríguez

> Steven A. Rodríguez helps founders build the systems, teams, and AI habits that turn chaos into momentum.

I'm Steven. I started with a curious mind in design, marketing and sales, politics, and systems thinking, and kept finding my way back to one job: helping people who start things get further, faster, and with less wasted effort.

That job has run through startup weekends, accelerator cohorts, and founder programs in many countries. Today it shows up as revenue systems, nearshore teams, and AI habits for small firms.

Steven writes and speaks for founders of 5-to-50-person firms on revenue systems, nearshore teams, and practical AI habits. Most of his writing is operator-focused book notes: each long summary links to short notes that turn one idea into a practice a team can try this week.

## Pages

- [Home](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/): Selected work, who Steven helps, field notes, speaking, and the newsletter.
- [About](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/about/): Background, the roles he has held, how he thinks about AI, speaking and mentoring, testimonials.
- [Writing](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/): Book summaries and the short notes that come out of them, grouped by book.
- [Speaker kit](https://stvnr.co/skit): Bio, headshots, and talk descriptions for event organizers.
- [Newsletter (Substack)](https://stvnrco.substack.com): Field notes by email. Free.

## Roles

- 2025 to now: Manager for Startups, Global Entrepreneurship Network. Startup programming for a global network, matching founders with partners, mentors, and resources.
- 2022 to 2023: Program Director, Tech Incubator at Queens College. Directed the accelerator for diverse tech founders, one of five operators in NYC's Founder Fellowship.
- 2021 to 2022: Director of Latinx Programs, New Majority Ventures (fmly 1863 Ventures). Grants, coaching, and community so New Majority businesses could recover, rebuild, and grow after COVID-19.
- 2019 to 2021: Regional Manager US/Canada, Startup Programs, Techstars. Supported the volunteer organizers behind Startup Weekend. Named 2020 CMX Community Professional of the Year.
- Earlier: Startup Weekend, Startup Leadership Program, Techstars DC Startup Week, Washington, D.C. startup ecosystem. Weekends, cohorts, and city-wide weeks that gave first-time founders a room and a team.

## Book summaries

- [Awaken the Giant Within — Summary, Key Lessons, and How to Use Them](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/awaken-the-giant-within-summary/): A builder's summary of Tony Robbins' book 'Awaken the Giant Within' — decisions, beliefs, the Master System, and how to actually use them.
- [How to Get Anything You Want: Elsie Lincoln Benedict on the Moods That Build Your Life](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/how-to-get-anything-you-want/): Elsie Lincoln Benedict's How to Get Anything You Want, in plain terms: how your predominant moods build your outer life — and how to remake them.
- [Earn the Right: A First-Time Founder's Guide to Starting a Startup](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/earn-the-right-starting-a-startup/): James Sinclair's Earn the Right framework in plain terms: prove the problem, win the market, and walk backwards from failure.

## Field notes

- [The Atomic ICP: Stop Trying to Boil the Ocean](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/atomic-icp-stop-boiling-the-ocean/): Aiming at everyone makes you invisible. James Sinclair wants one named persona with a budget and a wound — owned completely.
- [Clock Speed: The Fastest Learner Wins](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/clock-speed-fastest-learner-wins/): Forget polish. James Sinclair argues the founder who learns, iterates, and re-releases fastest is the one still standing.
- [Learned helplessness is the quiet killer](https://224-kringle-steverodrigz.netlify.app/blog/learned-helplessness/): The deadliest belief on a team is that effort won't move the score. Tony Robbins on learned helplessness and how to break it.
